summary: Context files can raise cost, anchor agents to stale interpretations, and create an opaque instruction hierarchy whose conflicts are harder to inspect than the source code.

points.text: Direct evaluation found no general success-rate improvement and more than 20% average inference-cost increase, so mandatory loading can be net negative.
Copied architecture summaries and command lists drift from build files and tests; their authoritative tone may discourage the agent from checking changed reality.
Organization, user, repository, directory, and task instructions can conflict. Silent precedence and branch-local instruction changes create prompt-injection and review risks.
Maintaining parallel files for multiple assistants duplicates policy and encourages lowest-common-denominator prose instead of stable links and machine-enforced rules.
